candidates.original_title: Melanoma genome sequencing reveals frequent PREX2 mutations
candidates.description: Expression of mutant PREX2 isoforms (G844D and Q1430*) decreases tumor-free survival compared to wild-type PREX2 and GFP controls in vivo
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 3B and S6 of Berger et al. (2012).
candidates.notes: [ling26: no entry matched this anchor] The replication found no significant differences in tumor-free survival between any groups (all Bonferroni-corrected p > 0.99). Control groups (GFP and PREX2[WT]) had dramatically shorter median TFS (1 week) compared to the original study (5 weeks for mutant groups), masking any potential PREX2 mutation effect. Meta-analyses of original and replication effects were all non-significant (p = 0.344–0.493). The authors frame the control group outcomes as fundamentally different from the original, preventing replication of the reported effect.

candidates.original_title: Melanoma genome sequencing reveals frequent PREX2 mutations
candidates.description: Expression of PREX2[G844D] in NRAS[G12D] melanocytes causes shorter tumor-free survival in mice than expression of GFP.
candidates.citation_sentence: As described in the Registered Report (Chroscinski et al., 2014), we attempted a replication of the experiments reported in Figures 3B and S6 of Berger et al. (2012).
candidates.notes: The replication found no statistically significant difference in tumor-free survival between GFP and PREX2[G844D] groups. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
